## Impact Assessment

- User impact: every operator who records a gate rejection on any run of any of the eight workflows: the run can neither proceed, complete, nor accept the correction the rejection asked for; the envelope prescribes a command that fails; the only forward path is a new run over a new input that repeats every completed phase. Concretely one operator today, on run-4c51600606df, with the corrections already applied on the tree and nothing to re-review them against.
- Business impact: no business-impact statement was supplied as an input; the reporter's own impact section (`E-001`) states that the CKA-06 change cannot be re-reviewed or closed. Severity below therefore rests on technical impact alone, and `Q-004` routes the business question.
- Technical impact: a correctness failure of the recovery contract rather than an availability fault: the classified action rollback is never executed, so the primary control path from a gate rejection back to its producing phase is unavailable; every rejection leaves two failure envelopes permanently open and a recovery ledger that cannot be resolved; the clearing action the runtime prescribes fails; the consumer commands cannot complete a rework round. No data is lost or corrupted: committed artifacts, the transition log, events, and the rejection rationale are intact and immutable.
- Blast radius: (1) the state model in runtime/state_engine.py, whose transition tables and idempotency binding apply to every work type in every workflow; (2) the recovery path in runtime/framework_runtime.py and runtime/recovery_policy.py, that is the classification of gate-rejection, the mapping of actions onto statuses, guard G4-GATE, and the envelope clearing action for awaiting_recovery_task, reached by every gate rejection and every successor blocked behind one; (3) the operator command surface next, dispatch, release, and gate, whose replay and refusal behaviour is what makes the state permanent; (4) the contract text now false in practice, the failure classification matrix and recovery sequence in config/execution-engine.md, the rollback rule in config/runtime.md, the Failure Recovery sections of all eight workflow specifications, and the clearing-command and repeatability claims in runtime/README.md; (5) the consumers omn_agent/fix_comments.py and omn_agent/update.py and the user guide sections describing them; (6) the run-status projection, which reads state items only and on a synthetic store projected Completed alongside a failed gate, so a rejection on a workflow's final gate may report the run complete, not observed on a real run and carried as `Q-003`; (7) persisted stranded state: every run that has recorded a gate rejection while this defect is present, today run-4c51600606df, holds open envelopes, an unresolved ledger, and a failed gate that a code fix alone will not advance, so those records are part of the radius and the fix strategy must say what becomes of them; (8) runtime/verify_multi_phase.py check M12 (`E-018`), a boundary the fix must keep true rather than a place the defect reaches.

## Root Cause Analysis

- Root cause statement: the recovery contract's rollback action has no executor and no representation in the state model: the Recovery Controller decides rollback but the runtime maps every non-retry verdict onto blocked or failed, the rejection branch moves the gate to failed and leaves the producing phase completed, both statuses are terminal with no outgoing transition and a completed item cannot be rebound to a new attempt, and so a gate rejection can only strand its successors behind a guard that no command clears while the envelope names a clearing command that cannot apply to either work item.
- Why detection failed earlier: runtime/verify_recovery.py induces only Validation Engine rejections (Runs A and B) and never a gate rejection, so the one recovery class whose action is rollback is the one it never exercises; runtime/verify_multi_phase.py check M13 asserts that completed to running is refused and records that as correct, with no companion check that a rollback classification yields a dispatchable target (`E-017`); tests/test_fix_comments.py and tests/test_update.py drive the consumers against a stub runtime that makes the fix phase pending and eligible by fiat on rejection, so the suite encodes the assumption instead of testing it; and the gap was written into runtime/README.md as known gap 3 in prose that no check reads and no defect tracked.

## Fix Strategy

- Proposed fix: conditional on `Q-001`, the architect's decision on how a committed phase is re-entered, the fix must make the rollback the contract already classifies actually executable and human-gated: a recorded rollback-authorisation from a listed non-producing owner of the rejected gate must turn the rejection into a dispatchable producing phase, the rollback target the matrix names, carrying the rejection rationale as correction input, and must lift the successor's G4-GATE block once the rebuilt evidence is re-assessed at the gate; the rejected decision, its rationale, its envelope, and the transition that recorded it must remain immutable in the store, the ledger, and the event stream; the new attempt must not overwrite the committed artifact, so check M12 stays true, by attempt-scoped artifact paths or an explicit supersession record; every failure envelope's clearing action must name a command that succeeds for the work item type and status it is attached to; no path may bypass a rejected gate without a recorded decision from a listed owner, and the gate command's decision values, the Producer Exclusion Rule, and the runner's approval requirement stay as they are; and the fix must state what becomes of runs already stranded, today run-4c51600606df, either by applying the same authorised rollback to a gate already failed or by closing the run as superseded with a recorded reason, which `Q-005` routes.
- Alternative options: (a) represent the rollback in the state model, for example a supersession status or transition that reopens a committed phase as attempt n plus 1 under its existing idempotency key while its prior completion record stands; this is the structural change and belongs to the architect. (b) Represent the rollback as a distinct recovery work item enqueued by the Recovery Controller, as the recovery sequence in config/execution-engine.md already describes, that re-runs the producing phase and re-arms the gate without touching the original items; it keeps the existing terminality guarantees but adds a work type the scheduler and the aggregator must learn. (c) Containment that can ship independently of either: make the clearing action, the option list, and next tell the truth for a gate rejection, naming the new run or abort path rather than a release command that fails; this removes the false prescription but leaves the contract unmet. (d) Declare archive-and-new-run the designed recovery, as omn_agent/update.py already does for a changed input; this repeats every completed phase and would require rewriting the classification matrix, the recovery sequence, and eight workflow specifications to stop promising a return, which is why the contract does not support it.
- Regression risk: high
- Regression scope: the terminality guarantee that every phase's completion path relies on, checked by M13 and by the payload rebinding refusal and replay detection in runtime/state_engine.py, which any new transition out of completed or failed touches directly; the immutability of committed artifacts under M12 and the completion package and provenance manifest that read each item's committed artifact path, which an attempt-scoped or superseding artifact changes; the scheduler in refresh and its distinction between guard-raised and recovery-raised blocks, shared with the validation-rejection repair path proven by verify_recovery Runs A and B; retry-budget accounting in attempts_charged and the release budget refusal, which a re-entered phase's new attempt is charged against; gate-policy auto-approval and its precedent lookup, which read recorded gate decisions and would see a re-armed gate; the consumers omn_agent/fix_comments.py and omn_agent/update.py and their stub-driven tests, which encode the status shape they expect after a rejection; the run-status projection and the aggregator's completion trigger, which read state item statuses; and the contract text in config/execution-engine.md, config/runtime.md, runtime/README.md, the eight workflow specifications, and docs/USER-GUIDE.md, which must describe whichever representation is chosen.

## Validation Plan

- Verification steps: invert the reproduction. Plan a run, complete a phase closed by a two-owner gate, record reject from the non-producing owner, then record the rollback authorisation the fix introduces from a listed owner: expect the producing phase to become pending and eligible and next to name it; the successor's G4-GATE block to clear when the gate is decided again over the rebuilt evidence; the re-dispatch to carry the rejection rationale in its input contract; the second attempt to commit an artifact without altering the first attempt's recorded digest, with verify_multi_phase M12 and M13 both proven on that run; the original rejection, its envelope, and transition to remain in state.json, recovery-ledger.json, and events.jsonl; no failure envelope on that run to name a clearing command that fails when executed; and the negative cases to hold, the producing role refused, an unlisted role refused, and no status change from rejected without a recorded human decision. Then run the pr fix-comments round against the real runtime rather than the stub and expect it to reach re-approval.
- Regression tests added: a third scenario in runtime/verify_recovery.py that induces a gate rejection on the real runtime and proves the authorised rollback, the immutability of the rejected evidence, and the M12 invariant across two attempts; a state-engine check extending M13 that whichever transitions the fix introduces are the only new legal ones and that completed and failed remain otherwise terminal; a check that every failure envelope's clearing action is executable for the work item type and status it is attached to; replacement of the fiat rejected stage in tests/test_fix_comments.py and tests/test_update.py with the real runtime's status shape after an authorised rollback; and the existing baseline, all tests and every verify script proven, with verify_recovery.py and verify_multi_phase.py named explicitly.
- Monitoring signals after release: the count of runs whose recovery ledger holds an open gate-rejection entry while no state item is pending and eligible and no gate is awaiting a decision, which should be zero; next exiting 3 with awaiting_recovery_task attributed to gate-rejection on any run, which should not recur; growth of replays_suppressed against completed phases on a run with a rejected gate, a leading sign that an operator is retrying dispatch into the stall; and any clearing action recorded in a failure envelope that returns RUNTIME FAILURE or NOTHING TO RELEASE when executed as written.

repositoryWrites.rationale: This is the only framework role that changes repository source. Its write scope cannot be enumerated per agent, because the files a change touches are named by the accepted design rather than by the manifest. The scope is therefore the repository, minus the evidence classes below, and every file actually written is declared in the change set and in the result envelope, where the runtime compares them.
repositoryWrites.exclusionRationale: Committed run evidence and governance records are immutable to the agents whose work they record. A run artifact this agent could edit would let a change rewrite the evidence assessed against it.

determinism.contract: Identical approved inputs and an identical context snapshot must produce the same change-set entry set, the same test-evidence set, the same deviation set, and the same declared verification status.
determinism.orderingRule: Change-set entries are ordered by the sequence in which the accepted design requires them; ties break toward the lower path in lexical order. Test-evidence entries follow the change-set entries they cover.
determinism.modelIndependence: No module may reference a specific model, vendor, or agent runtime. Technology names are permitted only when they trace to the supplied design, standards, or repository context.
